articles.title: I’m a semi-competitive shopper. These are my 12 favorite finds for someone who has everything
articles.summary: Thoughtful, elevated gifts for the person impossible to shop for on your list – from tea warmers to butter-shaped dishes. The nine best personalized gifts. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: The “has everything” person is, in some ways, the easiest person on your list to shop for: you know they like lip balm or bath salts or interesting spices, so why not get them more of those things and be done with it? Speaking as both a “has everything” person and a semi-competitive shopper, what I’m looking to get and give in this category is anything that solves a problem I didn’t know I had, anything that makes the most mundane parts of my day a little more special and anything that makes me laugh. I asked friends, relatives and experts to weigh in, and together we came up with 17 gifts that do all of those things and then some.

articles.title: All Accounted for After Tanker Crashes Into Docked New Orleans Riverboat
articles.summary: Gov. Jeff Landry of Louisiana called it a “literal miracle on the Mississippi” that all of the nearly 200 people aboard the riverboat were rescued.
body: A tanker ship struck a riverboat carrying 197 people on Friday in New Orleans, causing the cruise ship to capsize at its dock and prompting a wide-scale search-and-rescue operation, the authorities said.

Mayor Helena Moreno of New Orleans said at a news conference that all passengers of the riverboat, the American Heritage, were accounted for after the crash. A city of New Orleans spokesperson added that 32 people were at local hospitals, and one person had serious injuries.
“It is a literal miracle on the Mississippi,” said Gov. Jeff Landry of Louisiana, who also spoke at the news conference.
Capt. Melanie A. Burnham, commander of Sector New Orleans for the U.S. Coast Guard, praised the work of those who rescued the ship’s passengers.
points: Jeff Landry of Louisiana called it a “literal miracle on the Mississippi” that all of the nearly 200 people aboard the riverboat were rescued.

articles.title: Trump Administration Delays Enforcement of Medicaid Work Requirement
articles.summary: The federal government had planned to require poor adults to prove they were working or lose insurance coverage starting Jan. 1. Now, it will let states wait until July.
body: The Trump administration will allow states to delay enforcement of new rules requiring low-income adults to work in order to receive Medicaid coverage, according to a letter it sent on Friday to state Medicaid directors.

The announcement, which followed a recent loss in court over a key element of the work requirement, represents a major setback for a long-sought Republican reform. It comes less than two months before the work requirements were set to begin, on Jan. 1. States can now wait until July before ending coverage for people who do not meet the work requirement, the letter said.

In the letter, Dan Brillman, who oversees Medicaid at the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, acknowledged the significant burden states faced in building out new, expensive software systems to track the employment of enrollees. Hospitals have prepared massive education campaigns to help patients navigate the additional paperwork.
“We have heard directly from states about their implementation timelines, impediments to successful launches at scale,” Mr. Brillman wrote in the letter.

articles.title: She gets 16 pelvic exams a day – so yours don’t hurt
articles.summary: Molly Callahan, a gynecological teaching assistant, helps medical students practice pap smears and breast exams. On her busiest days, Molly Callahan, has 16 speculums inserted into her vagina.
body: It’s not as unpleasant as you might think. In fact, the point is to help students learn how to do it without causing discomfort. Contrary to common belief, pap smears – tests that screen for cervical cancer – don’t have to be painful.

Pap smears have reduced cervical cancer–related deaths by 86%, but many women avoid them due to confusion around guidelines, perceived lack of symptoms and, most commonly, speculum discomfort and embarrassment. One large study of US cancer statistics data found that from 2005 to 2023, 32% of women aged 21-29, and 15% of women aged 30-65, had never had a pap smear.

The negative association isn’t surprising. Looking at the cervix for indications of cancer became more common in the early 20th century, said Dr Kirsten Gardner, director of medical humanities at the University of Texas San Antonio, and methods centered innovation over comfort.

articles.title: NYC’s Secret Budget Hotel Hack: Religious Guesthouses
articles.summary: Staying near prime tourist attractions in Manhattan can cost hundreds, even thousands, of dollars a night. These five properties welcome budget travelers of any faith.
body: The Quaker-run Penington Friends House is in a brownstone on a quiet Gramercy Park street. Credit...

New York City never fails to shock visitors with its $28 cups of coffee, $34 hamburgers and dizzyingly expensive hotels. The average daily room rate reached a record $468.54 in September, according to the CoStar Group, a real estate analytics company.
But budget travelers who don’t mind spartan furnishings and shared bathrooms may find the answer to their prayers in the city’s religious guesthouses.

Most of these under-the-radar accommodations, often within walking distance of major attractions, welcome guests of any faith, or nonbelievers, at a fraction of the price of a hotel. And they come with an amenity few hotels can match: a sense of community.

articles.title: Branding it like Beckham: how Jude Bellingham is future-proofing his fame
articles.summary: From Calvin Klein to British Vogue, the Real Madrid man is leading the way when it comes to football’s foray into fashion. But is he playing it safe? This Sunday, Jude Bellingham will line up with his England teammates for a match against Spain.
body: It’s a savvy move for the 23-year-old, future-proofing himself as a power player both on and off the pitch. This is a roadmap carved out by David Beckham, who since retiring in 2013 has become a brand and personality that transcends sport. Beckham – together with his wife, Victoria – became a billionaire this year.

The Calvin Klein ads, which feature Bellingham in underwear, sometimes in his signature Christ the Redeemer pose, have caused a stir since appearing in London and New York, with passersby stopping to take selfies. The popularity of a billboard in Soho, New York also cements his celebrity status in the US after this summer’s World Cup.

Of course Bellingham is a bona fide star on the pitch. Mark Borkowski, a public relations consultant, says this factor is pivotal to the footballer’s crossover appeal. “Bellingham is an exceptional sporting talent, and his brand value is understandably enormous,” he says. “But fashion doesn’t create that value, football does. Fashion merely provides another means of exploiting it.”

articles.title: Kennedy’s Future: Will Democrats Try to Impeach Him, or Actually Work With Him?
articles.summary: Most Democrats abhor the health secretary’s stance on vaccines, but some see an opportunity to win voters from his MAHA movement by joining with him on food and environmental issues.
body: Sheryl Gay Stolberg covers Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and his MAHA movement.

Three days after last week’s “blue wave” election, Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. posted a warning on X to anyone suspecting his Make America Healthy Again movement had been weakened. “It’s time to unleash the Kraken,” he wrote.

The phrase, a reference to the 1981 movie “Clash of the Titans” that gained currency in 2020 among far-right internet personalities who claimed Democrats stole the election, suggests Mr. Kennedy will fight for his agenda and has no intention of leaving his job despite the defeat of several MAHA-backed candidates.
The question now is whether Democrats will use their new majorities in Congress to try to push him out.

articles.title: What Makes a Man of the Year? Inside GQ’s Big Night Out at the Chateau Marmont
articles.summary: GQ’s annual Men of the Year Party returned to Los Angeles, the first celebration under global editorial director Adam Baidawi, who was joined by co-hosts Chris Rock, Andrew Garfield, and Matt Damon; Director of the Year Denis Villeneuve; and Designer of the Year Michael Rider.
body: I pulled up to Chateau Marmont at 10 p.m. sharp, where hordes of photographers had congregated outside. Flashes were going off in rapid succession as I slipped out of my Uber in a pair of Marc Jacobs bow heels from the early 2010s with a giant smile on my face when not a single camera turned my way. I guess they don’t know good footwear when they see it.

I was there to cover GQ’s Men of the Year party—not to be confused with People’s Sexiest Man Alive, although I imagine there is some overlap in the tip sheets. This year, GQ was honoring not one man but five: Chris Rock, Andrew Garfield, Matt Damon, Celine’s Michael Rider, and legendary director Denis Villeneuve. Combine that with the guest list—Jason Bateman, Joshua Jackson, Travis Scott, Patrick Schwarzenegger, Miguel, Diplo, and Jordan Firstman to name a few—and it was quite the gathering of testosterone under one roof.

Try an 18th-century cottage surrounded by fields and wetlands for brisk winter walks; or perhaps a colorful jewel box apartment right in Stockholm (complete with a terrace, if you’re willing to brave the cold for your morning coffee). articles.title: How to Check Your Flight Status After the FAA Ordered Ground Stops for All Airports
articles.summary: On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop for all airports in the United States. If you're planning to fly this afternoon or evening, or you have friends or family doing the same, you're likely concerned about tracking flight statuses.
body: There are a number of options for tracking flights, whether you have your flight number or not. If you have the flight number, the fastest method is to Google it: Google will display a live tracker of your flight at the top of the results page. You can also head to the airline's official website to track your flight: United Airlines, for example, has a flight tracker where you can either enter your route information or your flight number. Most, if not all, airlines will have a similar tool you can use.

Alternatively, you can use a site or service that tracks all flights. FlightAware is one such site and has a flight tracker that lets you search flights—so long as you know the origin and the destination. If you have the flight number, your iPhone can help: You can enter your flight number into Spotlight search to see a live tracker, or you can text a contact your flight number, then tap the link that appears under the number to see a tracker of the flight.

articles.title: I’ve Finally Found Sunscreens for Oily Skin That Actually Stay Shine-Free
articles.summary: If greasiness is one of your main concerns, experts say the best sunscreen for oily skin is a matte-based mineral gel or lightweight sun serum for hydration and oil-control.
body: As a beauty editor, sunscreen is a near-daily topic of conversation, practically as commonplace as the weather. But when you have oily skin, finding the right formula isn’t about picking up the next new tube, but finding one that won’t slide off my face; or even worse, one that yields a breakout. Sometimes it feels like I can either protect my skin from UV rays or create a whole new set of skin problems.

Sunscreen remains one of the trickiest skin-care categories to get right when you have oily skin. You want something that protects your skin without feeling greasy, clogging pores, or pilling under makeup; a balance that board-certified dermatologist Marnie Nussbaum, MD knows all too well. “I always tell my patients that oily skin still needs hydration and daily sun protection, but I often get pushback because sunscreens can feel heavy or leave behind a greasy finish for those with oily skin.”

articles.title: Half Cruise, Half Cargo Ship? What It's Like to Sail French Polynesia Aboard a Local Freighter
articles.summary: Writer Scott Laird hops aboard a 12-night sailing with Aranui Cruises, a locally owned line that offers passenger and cargo services from Tahiti to the Marquesas Islands.
body: It’s certainly a romantic notion to hop a freighter and sail to the distant South Pacific. One could spend days at sea staring at nothing but seabirds and cargo pallets, waking up to the sound of those pallets being offloaded onto a tiny concrete wharf, meeting a community nestled among palms. One could take the day to hike or tour the island, or feast on fresh catches with the locals, while the offloaded pallets are filled with grapefruits, dried coconut husks, and flowers to be sold elsewhere— Tahiti, perhaps.

It might come as a surprise to know that one company has been offering dedicated cruises built around that very premise for over 40 years. In French Polynesia, the locally owned cruise line Aranui Cruises offers combination passenger and cargo services from Papeete, Tahiti, to the dramatically jagged volcanic pitons and pastoral scenes of the Marquesas Islands.
Fatu Hiva in the Marquesas Islands has no airport and is only accessible by sea.

articles.title: US Flights Have Been Grounded Nationwide
articles.summary: The rare ground stop does not apply to flights that are already airborne, according to United Airlines.
body: The United States Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a rare nationwide ground stop Friday afternoon, with all outbound flights from the US being directed to halt ground operations. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin stated in a press conference that there was “no indication as of yet” that anything “nefarious” caused the ground stop, and suggested that it due to a broad was a telecommunications outage.

“There has been a temporary telecommunications outage - out of an abundance of caution all flights have been halted,” the FAA said in a statement on X. “Every flight has been accounted for and international flights will be handled on a case by case basis.”
Department of Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a statement that the ground stop was due to a "communication issue" and that “FAA technicians are investigating.”
